report:
PASS for the scoped P15.1 continuation. The bounded theorem, the stated finite-energy extension, and the concentration counterexample are established. This does not establish original catalogue closure or any explicitly excluded stronger theorem. No filesystem or computational diagnostics were used as mathematical evidence.

The external foundations are listed below and were checked against opened primary sources. Their applications require neither a fibration nor a model reference, minimal singularities of the actual anchor, or a small unbounded locus.

Degree and masses. The current Tψ+εω dominates εω, so its class is big. A minimal-singularity current in that class is less singular than this actual current; DDNL monotonicity therefore bounds its top nonpluripolar mass by the class volume. The positive binomial expansion and boundary-volume limit imply Mn=0. Since M0>0, the maximum defining d exists and d<n. Pointwise comparison of two Kähler forms preserves every positivity test defining d. DDNL bounded-type mass equality applies with k current slots and n−k smooth Kähler slots, giving equation (6). Consequently every mixed product of degree greater than d has zero positive trace mass and is the zero current. Closedness and distributional Stokes establish the cohomological polynomial dependence of every Mk. These arguments include k=0, d=0, and n=1.

Signed products and gradients. Every current R used in the bounded proof is closed, positive, and of bidegree (n−1,n−1). Its trace measure does not charge the representation poles; when the nonpluripolar product is empty, R is smooth. Thus the bounded differences and smooth test functions satisfy Vu’s admissibility hypothesis. Iterated relative products identify the signed ddᶜ insertion with the difference of the two actual-current products. This identification also works for a nonpositive smooth background: add a sufficiently large smooth Kähler form to make the relevant currents positive, expand, and cancel the common smooth contribution.

The gradient correction is harmless for these applications because the argument actually reconstructs the calculation with the intrinsic definition ½ddᶜ(a²)−a ddᶜa. For the stated cutoff, bounded Stokes gives ∫dχk∧dᶜχk∧R=−∫χk ddᶜχk∧R≤4k⁻¹∫Ω∧R. The truncation gradients have the uniform bound 2‖ak‖∞∫Ω∧R. Cauchy–Schwarz therefore kills the cutoff cross terms. Locality identifies the remaining terms on {χk>0}, and finite signed-product and gradient masses justify dominated convergence. Symmetry, the negative diagonal identity, and polarization give (F) with its correct sign and factor. The page-6 square coefficients are indeed 1,1,−½. Vu’s convention conversion sends source potentials to u/2 and source gradient products to one half of the present ones; multiplying the source IBP equality by two yields exactly (F). DDNL potentials are rescaled by 1/(2π), preserving the actual currents.

Bounded energy. Multilinearity makes the finite-parameter one-form polynomial. Admissible IBP proves equality of its cross derivatives, so ordinary simplex Stokes establishes the segment primitive and cocycle. Its first variation is equation (9); its second variation is the negative integral of a positive admissible Dirichlet product, establishing concavity. Positivity establishes monotonicity, mixed mass equality gives the raw shift cMd, and the pointwise constant sandwiches give the Lipschitz estimate. Endpoint derivatives follow from polynomial continuity. The stated finite-simplex chain rules introduce no assertions about unbounded velocities. At d=0 the energy is affine and no gradient formula is needed.

Representative independence. The compact Kähler ddᶜ lemma supplies the smooth function g for two cohomologous auxiliary forms. Transferring ddᶜg to the bounded difference inserts one additional same-type current. Both resulting degree-(d+1) products vanish, proving equation (11), including d=0. The argument works one factor at a time for mixed auxiliary forms. Extension by differences of Kähler forms is well defined, and a fixed local linear choice of positive representatives proves homogeneous polynomial dependence on the auxiliary class. Simultaneous background changes preserve currents and differences; anchor changes have the cocycle rather than absolute independence.

Perturbation limits. The segment expansion proves equation (13) at every degree; the displayed subset-counting argument gives the coefficient binom(n,k)/(k+1), including k=0. Equation (14) follows from the bounded difference and the common mixed mass. For class-convergent auxiliary representatives, the cohomological Mk remain bounded in a neighborhood of the limiting Kähler class. Hence Pε=O(ε^(n−d)) without any representative bounds. The moving-potential error is at most δεPε, while each normalized lower coefficient is O(ε^(d−k)). Polynomial class continuity handles the leading coefficient. This proves (15) under precisely its bounded-type and uniform-convergence hypotheses. It does not imply representative independence of the full perturbed energy; the smooth product example correctly exhibits a changing lower coefficient.

The differential-measure assertions have their separate hypotheses. For fixed u and ω, the measure expansion proves (16). Factoring the moving top-product difference, applying admissible IBP against a smooth test, and inserting one smooth ω slot give (17), with Qε=O(ε^(n−d−1)). The normalized error is O(δε/ε), so δε=o(ε) suffices. Smoothly converging auxiliary forms provide uniform test bounds and convergence of smooth multiplication. Class-only convergence supplies neither of these measure conclusions, and the argument correctly makes no such claim.

Finite-energy domain. With m=d, P=Tψ, smooth relative current ω^(n−d), and linear weight, equation (17a) is exactly Vu’s joint weighted class after normalization by constants and the positive convention rescaling. Connectedness makes equality of top-degree cohomology classes equivalent to equality of masses. Convexity applies to the average of any finite family. Every ordered mixed mass is at most M by slotwise monotonicity, and their average equals M; therefore every mixed mass equals M. Expanding the finite diagonal weighted integral of that average, together with ψ−ui≤N(ψ−w), proves every mixed weight-integrability assertion needed for the extension and cocycle. Degree-greater-than-d vanishing for more-singular potentials follows separately by monotonicity. No lower-degree weighted estimate follows from this argument, and none is asserted.

Truncation and continuity. On the strict comparison set, locality identifies the truncated and original mixed measures. Their equal total masses identify the complementary masses, where the truncated weight is exactly L. Thus equation (21a) is an exact identity, including comparison boundaries, and monotone convergence proves the truncation limit. The bounded decreasing-continuity lemma uses uniformly bounded local psh truncations and bounded quasicontinuous weights, so DDNL Proposition 2.2 applies locally. Equal total masses control the omitted polar-locus tails. The squeeze between E(u) and the energy of max(vj,ψ−L), followed first by j→∞ and then L→∞, proves continuity for every stated decreasing sequence with a domain limit. Convexity and simultaneous bounded truncations then prove concavity.

The finite-energy cocycle is also justified term by term. Simultaneous truncations agree with the original mixed products on GL and have the same complementary mass. Their tail contribution is bounded by ∫BL(zu+zv)dνa, which tends to zero by the previously established mixed integrability. Passing the bounded cocycle to the limit proves (20a). The same estimates justify changing the bounded-type anchor. Closedness preserves the scalar full-mass condition under cohomologous auxiliary changes, pointwise comparison preserves weighted finiteness, and the bounded truncation energies preserve their values. This proves the stated domain and energy representative independence. For d=0, smooth-volume local integrability supplies the domain conditions directly, and the same truncation arguments apply.

Examples and retained data. The radial potential has positive singular Laplacian, vanishing point flux, and weighted singular integral proportional to ∫∞t^(2a−2)dt; this is finite exactly in the asserted range 0<a<½. The cutoff error has bounded Hessian on a fixed annulus and is dominated by κ for sufficiently small b. Thus the example is an actually unbounded domain member. In the concentration example, every auxiliary form is smooth and Kähler in the same class, every fixed-parameter weighted integral is finite, and the perturbed top mass equals the anchor mass 2ε(1+ε). Direct expansion gives (24a). Since the bump is supported where −v≥bε⁻², its normalized lower coefficient tends to −∞. A fixed smooth representative gives the finite leading limit instead. This establishes the advertised failure of the unbounded auxiliary-path strengthening while respecting all its claimed full-mass and finite-energy properties.

The reference-scale quotient is valid at its stated bounded-family scope: factorwise representative independence defines the multilinear functionals, and their common kernel gives exactly the equivalence relation for all bounded relative energies. It supplies no geometric quotient or universal unbounded minimum reference. The constant-shift example proves necessary scale dependence. The divisor reference has degree zero in the same nef class whose smooth reference has degree one; its actual perturbation mass and class-volume leading powers differ. The carrier statements correctly retain X, the degree-d current, and complementary smooth factors.

Harmless qualifications should be recorded explicitly. First, GZ Proposition 3.7 is printed for bounded potentials. The general scalar decreasing-capacity statement follows by truncating at −L, applying that bounded proposition, and bounding the omitted set by Proposition 3.6; Proposition 3.10 transfers the capacity control to local charts. Thus the citation should name these accompanying results. Second, Vu Theorem 3.3 has bounded product factors and possibly unbounded comparison potentials; its use for nonpluripolar products is justified by applying it to bounded local truncations and then exhausting the finite loci. Third, the cutoff’s ‘support’ should mean its nonzero locus when asserting containment in strict truncation sets. Finally, the annexed BEGZ Lemma 1.5 cannot be used for arbitrary non-exhausting sequences merely because their union has pluripolar complement: alternating empty sets would contradict that wording. The relevant sets here increase, or the cutoffs converge pointwise to one, so dominated convergence establishes every actual use. These qualifications do not require a new substantive argument or change a scoped conclusion.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-manifold, closed positive (1,1)-currents S1,…,Sp, with 1≤p≤n, have a finite closed positive nonpluripolar product ⟨S1⋯Sp⟩. These products are symmetric, multilinear on positive sums, depend only on the currents, are plurifinely local, have trace measures charging no pluripolar sets, and agree with ordinary multiplication for smooth positive factors. For locally bounded psh potentials, the underlying Bedford–Taylor products support decreasing approximation, bounded product calculus, and the chain rule d(f(v)R)=f′(v)dv∧R for smooth f and closed positive R. [BEGZ, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and 1.6, Theorem 1.8, Lemma 1.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).
passages.quote: The resulting positive (p, p)-current hT1 ∧...∧Tpi puts no mass on pluripolar subsets. It is also shown to be closed (Theorem 1.8), generalizing a classical result of Skoda-El Mir.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-manifold, closed positive (1,1)-currents S1,…,Sm and a closed positive (p,p)-current R, with m+p≤n, have a well-defined finite closed positive relative nonpluripolar product ⟨S1⋯Sm dot∧R⟩. It charges no locally complete pluripolar set on which R has no mass; it is additive in a positive current slot when R charges neither relevant polar locus; and iterating relative products gives the same product. With a smooth closed positive relative factor W, these products coincide with ordinary nonpluripolar products multiplied by W. Signed ddᶜ products of admissible differences are differences of the corresponding relative products. [Vu, §2 and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

passages.statement: Let X be compact Kähler, P=θ+ddᶜφ a closed positive (1,1)-current, 1≤m≤n, and W a smooth closed positive (n−m,n−m)-form. Among currents S=θ+ddᶜu cohomologous to P and more singular than P, the relative full-mass space defined by {⟨S^m dot∧W⟩}={⟨P^m dot∧W⟩} is convex. Its joint linear-weight subclass, defined after shifting u≤φ by finiteness of m∑a=0^m binom(m,a)∫(φ−u)⟨S^aP^(m−a) dot∧W⟩, is convex and unchanged when P is replaced by a cohomologous current of the same bounded singularity type. Weighted finiteness is independent of additive potential constants. P need not have minimal or model singularities. [Vu, equation (3.1), Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).
passages.quote: Theorem 3.4. For χ ∈ W − , the sets Eχ,m,P (T ) and Em,P (T ) are convex.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold with a fixed smooth lower Hessian bound, a decreasing sequence of quasi-psh functions with a quasi-psh limit not identically −∞ converges in Kähler Monge–Ampère capacity. Quasi-psh functions are quasicontinuous. For a fixed negative Ω-psh function φ, CapΩ({φ<−L})≤Cφ/L; global Kähler capacity is comparable to Bedford–Taylor capacities on a finite collection of relatively compact coordinate subdomains. The general decreasing assertion follows from the bounded decreasing assertion and this sublevel estimate. [Guedj–Zeriahi, Propositions 3.6–3.7, Corollary 3.8 and Proposition 3.10](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/JGA05.pdf).

passages.statement: Let U⊂C^n be open. Suppose f_j are uniformly bounded quasicontinuous functions converging in capacity to a quasicontinuous f, and, in every slot i=1,…,n, uniformly bounded psh functions u_i^j converge in capacity to u_i. Then f_j ddᶜu_1^j∧⋯∧ddᶜu_n^j converges weakly to f ddᶜu_1∧⋯∧ddᶜu_n, with the same conclusion after a fixed positive normalization change of ddᶜ. [DDNL, Proposition 2.2](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).
passages.quote: Proposition 2.2. Let 𝛺 ⊂ Cn be an open set. Suppose { f j } j are uniformly bounded quasicontinuous functions which converge in capacity to another quasicontinuous function f on 𝛺.

passages.statement: Let U⊂C^n be open, R a closed positive current, and a_i,a_i′ bounded psh functions for i=1,…,m, with the products of admissible degree. Let b_j,b_j′ be possibly unbounded psh functions for j=1,…,q, and W=⋂j{b_j>b_j′}. If a_i=a_i′ on W in every slot, then 1_W ddᶜa_1∧⋯∧ddᶜa_m∧R=1_W ddᶜa_1′∧⋯∧ddᶜa_m′∧R. On a compact Kähler n-manifold, closed positive (1,1)-currents S1,…,Sm and a closed positive (p,p)-current R, with m+p≤n, have a well-defined finite closed positive relative nonpluripolar product ⟨S1⋯Sm dot∧R⟩. It charges no locally complete pluripolar set on which R has no mass; it is additive in a positive current slot when R charges neither relevant polar locus; and iterating relative products gives the same product. With a smooth closed positive relative factor W, these products coincide with ordinary nonpluripolar products multiplied by W. Signed ddᶜ products of admissible differences are differences of the corresponding relative products. [Vu, §2 and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

Let X be compact Kähler, R a closed positive (n−1,n−1)-current, and a,b bounded R-admissible dsh functions: each has a representation as a difference of quasi-psh functions whose polar sets have zero R-mass. Their intrinsic relative Dirichlet products are finite and independent of the representation, the diagonal product is positive, and ∫b⟨ddᶜa dot∧R⟩=∫a⟨ddᶜb dot∧R⟩=−∫⟨db∧dᶜa dot∧R⟩. For differences of bounded quasi-psh functions, the diagonal definition is ½ddᶜ(a²)∧R−a ddᶜa∧R; bounded Stokes and Cauchy–Schwarz apply to these products. [Vu, equation (2.3), Lemmas 2.4–2.6 and Theorem 2.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

On a compact Kähler manifold, two cohomologous smooth closed real (1,1)-forms differ by ddᶜg for a smooth real function g, for any fixed positive normalization of ddᶜ. [Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan, §5, Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dennis/publications/PDF/DS-pub-0024.pdf).

Let X be compact Kähler, P=θ+ddᶜφ a closed positive (1,1)-current, 1≤m≤n, and W a smooth closed positive (n−m,n−m)-form. Among currents S=θ+ddᶜu cohomologous to P and more singular than P, the relative full-mass space defined by {⟨S^m dot∧W⟩}={⟨P^m dot∧W⟩} is convex. Its joint linear-weight subclass, defined after shifting u≤φ by finiteness of m∑a=0^m binom(m,a)∫(φ−u)⟨S^aP^(m−a) dot∧W⟩, is convex and unchanged when P is replaced by a cohomologous current of the same bounded singularity type. Weighted finiteness is independent of additive potential constants. P need not have minimal or model singularities. [Vu, equation (3.1), Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

On a compact Kähler manifold with a fixed smooth lower Hessian bound, a decreasing sequence of quasi-psh functions with a quasi-psh limit not identically −∞ converges in Kähler Monge–Ampère capacity. Quasi-psh functions are quasicontinuous. For a fixed negative Ω-psh function φ, CapΩ({φ<−L})≤Cφ/L; global Kähler capacity is comparable to Bedford–Taylor capacities on a finite collection of relatively compact coordinate subdomains. The general decreasing assertion follows from the bounded decreasing assertion and this sublevel estimate. [Guedj–Zeriahi, Propositions 3.6–3.7, Corollary 3.8 and Proposition 3.10](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/JGA05.pdf).

Let U⊂C^n be open. Suppose f_j are uniformly bounded quasicontinuous functions converging in capacity to a quasicontinuous f, and, in every slot i=1,…,n, uniformly bounded psh functions u_i^j converge in capacity to u_i. Then f_j ddᶜu_1^j∧⋯∧ddᶜu_n^j converges weakly to f ddᶜu_1∧⋯∧ddᶜu_n, with the same conclusion after a fixed positive normalization change of ddᶜ. [DDNL, Proposition 2.2](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).

Let U⊂C^n be open, R a closed positive current, and a_i,a_i′ bounded psh functions for i=1,…,m, with the products of admissible degree. Let b_j,b_j′ be possibly unbounded psh functions for j=1,…,q, and W=⋂j{b_j>b_j′}. If a_i=a_i′ on W in every slot, then 1_W ddᶜa_1∧⋯∧ddᶜa_m∧R=1_W ddᶜa_1′∧⋯∧ddᶜa_m′∧R. [Vu, Theorem 3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

Vu’s Relative non-pluripolar product of currents, arXiv:2004.11111v1, uses dᶜ=i/(2π)(∂̄−∂) and ddᶜ=i/π ∂∂̄. DDNL’s 2018 paper represents θ-psh currents as θ+i∂∂̄u. [Vu, notation and convention](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1), [DDNL, introductory definitions](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).
